summary: Intermittent 429s during large compressed upload triggered by orchestrator burst window oscillation
description: Issue summary: Customer sees intermittent 429 responses for a subset of large .zip batch uploads orchestrated by their background worker. The pattern is time-of-day aligned (daily midnight sync) and correlates with a short-lived spike in orchestrator fanout during a metadata refresh. Impact: ~7% of file uploads failing with 429 over a 25-minute window; user reports retry storms and duplicate partial uploads. This is a customer-facing support request for guidance and mitigation while we investigate root cause.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs nightly orchestrator job that breaks a large dataset into ~600 concurrent upload sessions (multipart) using signed URLs and ephemeral keys
2) Upload sessions start at 00:02 UTC and complete over ~15 minutes under normal conditions
3) During the observed window the orchestrator spikes extra preflight probes and health-check pings to verify node liveness, increasing simultaneous short-lived sessions
4) Approximately 6-8% of sessions get immediate 429 responses from the upload endpoint; retries escalate and some clients surface as failed to end-users
observed_behavior: Short (~25m) window where a subset of multipart upload attempts receive 429 with Retry-After absent or inconsistent; console shows tenant quota depletion despite allocated dedicated burst pool. Rate-limit headers when present show X-Rate-Limit-Remaining=0 for route-level buckets but tenant-level tokens still appear available in some telemetry snapshots.
expected_behavior: Large orchestrated uploads should consume burst tokens from the dedicated burst pool and receive consistent Retry-After headers when throttled; background health checks should not count against route burst windows or should be allocated to a separate background pool.

comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Sana Mehta: Added initial logs and described nightly sync pattern. Customer confirms the orchestrator runs an explicit metadata reconciliation before upload wave.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Luis Ortega: I can reproduce locally with a scaled-down orchestrator sim (200 short-lived preflight probes + 400 uploads) — seeing route-level remaining drop to 0 while tenant bucket still shows tokens. Suspect route-level smoothing window misalignment with burst pool assignment.

2026-03-11 02:21 - SRE (Marta Ivanov): Correlated with an autoscaler scale-in event for the dedicated pool at 00:08 which triggered health-check retries from the orchestrator. Health checks were counted against route buckets due to proxy affinity change after scale-in. Opening INT follow-up to evaluate probe exemption: INT-911.

2026-03-12 15:33 - Support (Luis Ortega): Temporary mitigation applied for customer: enabled split-route burst pool for files.uploads and configured their orchestrator to route health-checks to /internal-health which is exempt from tenant route accounting. Customer asked for long-term fix and confirmation of accounting rules.
2026-03-12 16:05 - ParcelFlow (Customer): Confirmed immediate drop in 429s after mitigation; asked for a short doc describing recommended orchestrator probe pattern and ideal retry/backoff settings.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: short-lived scale-in triggered health-check replay from the orchestrator which was multiplexed on the same route making the route-level token window oscillate. Route-level buckets are short-window and can be exhausted by many tiny probes even if tenant-level tokens remain; probes can then amplify retries from the orchestrator. Evidence: scale-in timestamp aligns with spike; proxy affinity change log shows requests counted on route:files:uploads. Preliminary reproduction in staging matches behavior when probe concurrency & timing mimic production.
actions_taken: 1) Temporarily provisioned a separate route burst pool for files.uploads for this tenant; 2) Advised customer to add jitter and exponential backoff to upload retries and to route health probes to an exempt endpoint; 3) Opened INT-911 to adjust proxy accounting exemption for internal-health endpoints during autoscaler events; 4) Added a console alert for route-level bucket depletion to surface to on-call earlier.
resolution: Workaround implemented and validated on 2026-03-12 — split-route burst pool prevented further 429s during nightly sync. Long-term: engineering to implement probe exemption on scale events (INT-911) and add documentation for orchestrator best-practices. Ticket will remain open until INT-911 is resolved and a post-change validation is completed.
next_steps: 1) Track INT-911 progress and validate in next scheduled canary (owner: Marta Ivanov)
2) Publish short customer-facing KB with recommended probe/backoff config and signed-url usage guidance (owner: Luis Ortega)
3) Add automated test that simulates scale-in + orchestrator probe fanout to catch regressions (owner: infra-test)
